title: What Is Kief?
seoTitle: What Is Kief? A Plain-English Guide | Uforia Dispensary
description: Kief is the fine, resin-rich powder of trichome heads that collects in a grinder's bottom chamber. Learn where it comes from and how people use it.
lede: If you have ever opened the bottom of a grinder and found a layer of fine, sandy powder, you have already met kief. It is one of the simplest cannabis concentrates there is, and it comes straight from the flower itself.

sections.heading: Where kief comes from
sections.html:
Look closely at a cannabis bud and you will notice that it sparkles. That frosty coating is made of trichomes, tiny glands that cover the flowers and the small leaves around them. Each trichome has a slender stalk topped with a rounded head, and that head is where the plant stores most of its resin.

The resin holds the plant's cannabinoids, such as THC and CBD, along with the terpenes that give each strain its aroma. When dried flower is handled, shaken or ground, many of those trichome heads snap off. Gathered together, the loose heads are what people call kief.

Kief looks like a fine powder, anywhere from pale green to golden tan. The more finely it is sifted, the lighter it tends to be, because less leafy plant matter comes along with it.

sections.heading: How a grinder collects it
sections.html:
Most people collect kief without even trying. A three-chamber grinder, often sold as a four-piece grinder, has a fine mesh screen above its bottom compartment. As you grind, the broken-up flower stays in the middle chamber, while the smallest particles, mostly trichome heads, sift through the screen and settle below.

With regular use, that bottom chamber slowly fills over weeks or months. Keeping the screen clean lets it collect evenly, and a gentle tap on the table after grinding can shake a little more loose. Many grinders come with a small scraper for gathering it; use it softly so the mesh does not tear.

sections.heading: Ways people use kief
sections.html:
Because kief is more concentrated than the flower it fell from, people usually reach for it in small amounts. A few common ways to enjoy it:

  • Sprinkled on flower. A light dusting on top of a bowl or inside a joint is the most popular use by far.
  • Pressed into hash. With gentle warmth and pressure, kief can be pressed into a small, solid piece of hash.
  • In a vaporizer. Many dry herb vaporizers handle kief well, often with a small pad or screen so the powder does not slip through.
  • In homemade edibles. Kief can be infused into butter or oil, but it needs to be heated first, a step called decarboxylation that turns THCA into THC.

sections.heading: Strength, storage and a gentle note
sections.html:
Kief carries the same compounds as the flower it came from, just with less plant material in the way, so many people find a small pinch feels noticeably stronger than the same amount of flower. Its character also depends on what you have been grinding: a grinder that has seen several strains will hold a little of each.

If kief is new to you, start low and go slow. Use a small amount, give it time, and notice how you feel before adding more. To keep its aroma, store collected kief in a small airtight container away from heat and light.

Curious about other concentrates? Our guide to live resin and rosin explains two popular styles, and you can browse the concentrates on Uforia's live menu.

takeaways: Kief is the fine powder of trichome heads that falls away from dried cannabis flower.
A three-chamber grinder collects it in a screened bottom compartment.
People sprinkle it on flower, press it into hash or use it in a vaporizer.
Kief is more concentrated than flower, so start low and go slow.
